run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Within the only sampled interval available (cluster telemetry in this environment begins ~15:33:20, window ends 15:33:41), the cart workload was broken. Pod cart-74587775fc-ct6pb entered CrashLoopBackOff (restartCount 3 rising to 5, last termination reason Error, exitCode 139, no readiness/liveness/startup probes) and logged 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' from ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected()/Initialize(). Deployment cart was the only one of 23 deployments with zero available replicas, and the cart Service 10.96.143.45:8080 held only a notReadyAddress for that pod, so callers saw ECONNREFUSED: frontend returned HTTP 500 on /api/cart and /api/checkout, checkout's oteldemo.CartService/GetCart failed with gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE and PlaceOrder with 13, and the load-generator saw 100% failure on those endpoints. The cart pod's dependency was checked: valkey-cart was running, ready, restartCount 0, logged 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 15:32:26, had a ready Service endpoint, and the failing cart pod's own wait-for-valkey-cart init container reached 10.96.255.132:6379 at 15:33:20 - so TCP reachability existed while the cart app still could not establish its Redis session. The previous cart pod was serving normally until 15:33:17 and received a 'Stopping container cart' (Killing) at 15:33:18 with no ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete, i.e. an external deletion; the unchanged-template replacement then crashlooped for about three minutes before recovering (container running since 15:36:30). Who deleted the pod and the exact reason the Redis handshake failed remain unknown, so the conclusion is partial: cart is the failing component with evidenced downstream effects, but the fault-application object is not visible in the available sources.

claims.text: Deployment cart had zero ready/available replicas and a False Available condition with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, while every other deployment in astronomy-shop reported available=1.

Pod cart-74587775fc-ct6pb container 'cart' was not ready: state waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 40s restarting failed container=cart'), restartCount 3 and lastState.terminated reason 'Error' with exitCode 139; the container requests/limits memory 160Mi and defines no readiness, liveness or startup probe.

The crashloop persisted: at 15:34:58 the cart container had restartCount 4 with last termination reason Error, exitCode 139, startedAt 15:34:57 and finishedAt 15:34:58, and state waiting CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 1m20s').

Cart application logs at 15:33:22 show 'fail: cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore[0]' followed by 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' and 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' with stack frames cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() at ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 101 and ValkeyCartStore.Initialize() at line 71.

The cart Service (ClusterIP 10.96.143.45, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart) had only a notReadyAddress (10.244.125.28, pod cart-74587775fc-ct6pb); every other service endpoint in the namespace had ready addresses, including valkey-cart at 10.244.7.195:6379.

Frontend spans in traces 40c1c6dbb706d5e7faf1a5f72fa818ea, dddd1be569e98e535461856843e9e43c and 70091ef0a4f94d65b27de0d65e4e540e record HTTP 500 on POST /api/checkout and GET/POST /api/cart with exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.143.45:8080'.

Checkout's own spans fail on its cart dependency: oteldemo.CartService/GetCart spans (e.g. 46004d6de5a80d27, b1cef4382e614223, 065ba674e312c55d) carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=14 with 'dial tcp 10.96.143.45:8080: connect: connection refused', and the parent oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans fail with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout'.

load-generator and frontend-proxy spans in the same traces carry error=true with http.status_code=500 on POST /user traffic (load-generator span 4d3030050cf182b8; frontend-proxy spans 7ad021313dcf47ae and 1e4865d83644e268).

The previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-rv7hq was serving cart operations (GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync with ValkeyCartStore) up to 15:33:17, then received a Pod Killing event 'Stopping container cart' at 15:33:18; ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc created cart-74587775fc-ct6pb at 15:33:18 and the cart container was Created/Started three times between 15:33:20 and 15:33:35, with no ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete for the old pod.

The replacement pod ran an unchanged cart template: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-cart, env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, CART_PORT=8080, memory limit 160Mi, owned through ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc by Deployment cart; the live pod spec matches the Deployment template.

Pod cart-74587775fc-ct6pb's init container wait-for-valkey-cart reported 'valkey-cart (10.96.255.132:6379) open' at 15:33:20, i.e. DNS resolution and TCP reachability to the valkey-cart Service existed from the same pod whose cart container then failed to connect to Redis.

valkey-cart was running and ready with restartCount 0 and a 64Mi memory limit, and its log shows normal startup ('Valkey version=9.0.1', 'Running mode=standalone, port=6379', 'Ready to accept connections tcp') at 15:32:26 with no error lines in the sampled window.

All fault-injection settings in ConfigMap flagd-config (data key demo.flagd.json) have defaultVariant 'off': cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, failedReadinessProbe, imageSlowLoad, llmInaccurateResponse, llmRateLimitError are 'off' and kafkaQueueProblems/loadGeneratorFloodHomepage/emailMemoryLeak are 0.
The crashloop ended without any configuration change: at the last observation the cart container was running since 15:36:30 with restartCount 5 and ready=true, i.e. the fifth start succeeded.

Alerting rules evaluated after the sampled window (evaluation around 15:37) show the incident still active on this workload and its callers: PodStatusError for pod cart-74587775fc-ct6pb reason CrashLoopBackOff (activeAt 15:36:09), KubePodNotReady for the same pod (activeAt 15:35:09), HighRequestErrorRate frontend 19.72%, frontend-proxy 21.19%, checkout 66.67% pending, and locust endpoint failure ratio 1.00 on POST /api/checkout, GET /api/cart and POST /api/cart.

valkey-cart, the dependency named in cart's error, showed its own healthy signals: running and ready with 0 restarts, normal Redis startup log, a ready Service endpoint, and a successful TCP connect from the failing cart pod's init container - so the evidence does not show valkey-cart itself failing.

Other workloads were checked and found ready during the window: all 23 deployments except cart reported available=1 (including valkey-cart), and every container in astronomy-shop except cart's had ready status with 0 restarts at 15:33:44.

Memory-limit exhaustion (OOMKill) of the cart container was rejected: the last termination reason is 'Error' with exitCode 139 (not OOMKilled), no OOM/Eviction event was recorded for the pod in the event groups examined, and the cart container's working set was about 2.46 MB against a 160Mi limit at 15:33:41.

A switched-on flagd fault flag (cartFailure or failedReadinessProbe) was rejected as the cause: both flags exist but have defaultVariant 'off', as do all other demo fault flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap.

Cart Service/endpoint misconfiguration was rejected: the Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart matches the pod, port 8080 targets container port 8080, and the Endpoints object contains the pod (as a notReadyAddress), so the refused connections follow from the container being unready, not from wrong routing labels or ports.

The cart application's Redis session establishment failed transiently between 15:33:20 and 15:36:30 (DNS resolution or application-level handshake, since raw TCP to 10.96.255.132:6379 worked from the same pod), aborting every container start with the unhandled ApplicationException; the fifth start at 15:36:30 succeeded, which fits a transient per-pod condition rather than a persistent misconfiguration. The exact failure mode (resolution error vs. connect timeout) is not visible in the logs available inside the window.

An alternative candidate that remains open is that valkey-cart's Redis was temporarily unresponsive at the protocol level while still accepting TCP connections (which would explain the init container's successful nc check alongside the cart client's failure); this is unverified because valkey-cart's log shows only startup lines and no client-side errors, and the cadvisor sample for it exists only at 15:33:30.

The immediate trigger of the replacement pod was an external deletion of cart-74587775fc-rv7hq at 15:33:18 (Pod Killing 'Stopping container cart' with no ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete, and the same ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc creating the replacement); that deletion did not change the pod template, but the replacement then crashlooped, which is what actually made cart unavailable.

Read the cart container's StackExchange.Redis exception detail lines for restarts 2-5 (they fall after the authorized window) and, if the failure recurs, verify in-pod DNS resolution of valkey-cart and direct IP:6379 protocol access from the cart container to separate DNS from connection-refused/timeout failure modes.

Because the pod deletion at 15:33:18 is not attributable to any visible controller, check audit logs or chaos-injection records (not available in this run) to identify which actor deleted cart-74587775fc-rv7hq, and consider a startup probe plus connect-retry tolerance so a transient Redis connect failure cannot take the cart Service to zero endpoints.

gaps: The object or actor that deleted pod cart-74587775fc-rv7hq at 15:33:18 is unknown: the Killing event has no matching ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete, no chaos-related CRD was returned, and the change_history integration is not available in this run.

The exact reason the cart container's Redis connection failed is unknown: the logged exception details for restarts 2-5 and the current container's stdout fall after the authorized window end (15:33:41), and only 14 log lines of pod cart-74587775fc-ct6pb were inside the window.
Whether valkey-cart's Redis was briefly unresponsive at the protocol level could not be verified; its in-window log contains only startup lines and its first cadvisor sample is at 15:33:30.
No pre-incident baseline exists: traces start at 15:33:20.188 and the first complete metric sample is 15:33:41, so no trend or comparison with an earlier healthy period can be made.
The NetworkPolicy query returned no objects (status no_data), so the absence of a policy blocking cart->valkey-cart traffic is not established.

The Prometheus instant queries for restart counts and last-terminated reasons in the astronomy-shop namespace returned no data (status no_data), so pod restart history from kube-state-metrics is unavailable; restarts were read from the pod objects instead.

Trace data is a sampled projection: the cart service trace search for 15:33:20-15:33:41 returned no data, and span counts are not unique request counts, so the blast radius among callers is stated only for the operations whose own error spans were observed.

The traces_span_metrics_calls_total series in this environment carried only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET and covered a small subset of services, so per-service error-rate series could not be used; error evidence came from spans, logs, pod status and alert state.
next_steps: Read the cart container's post-window logs (restarts 2-5 and the current instance from 15:36:30) to capture the StackExchange.Redis exception detail and confirm DNS vs. timeout vs. connection-refused.
Check cluster audit logs or the fault-injection controller's records for who deleted pod cart-74587775fc-rv7hq at 2026-11-21T15:33:18Z.
If the symptom returns, run a DNS lookup and a redis protocol check (PING) from inside the cart container against valkey-cart to discriminate a DNS problem from an unresponsive server.
Review cart client settings (connect-abort/retry policy) and add a startup probe so transient dependency failures during start do not remove all cart endpoints.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
